# KyberNow

> KyberNow is free, open-source (AGPL-3.0) remote play and remote desktop: install KyberNow Station on your Windows PC, your Apple-silicon Mac or your Linux machine, then play and work on it from all your devices with KyberNow Link, in a native app or in a web browser. The same apps also play a PS5 or PS4 on your network, and KyberNow Share lets guests watch or play with you and lets you lend the computer to family, friends or a team. It serves two audiences: players (remote play on the TV, a tablet, a Steam Deck, a browser) and professionals (creatives, remote workstations, game studios, teams and fleets). It is an alternative to Sunshine + Moonlight, built on the Kyber streaming engine (by VLC developers) and the QUIC protocol. Currently in beta (0.x versions, not yet 1.0).

Key facts:

- **What it is**: self-hosted, "your own cloud". Unlike cloud gaming services, nothing is rented. At home the picture goes straight from the PC to your devices, with no server in between. Away from home, your devices reach the PC through KyberNow's relay (an Admin setting, "Access away from home", off by default; the public relay share.kybernow.app is open to everyone, and you can install your own) or through a VPN (Tailscale, WireGuard); the PC must be switched on. In the apps, the picture, the sound and the keystrokes stay encrypted end to end through the relay, which sees addresses, bitrates and share codes; a browser is the exception, as the relay decrypts its traffic to forward it.
- **Latency**: 9.4 ms median from capture to display, measured on 19 October 2026 with the Kyber 0.29 engine and its own client (RTX 3080 Ti PC to a MacBook Pro M4 Max, local network, H.264). With KyberNow's virtual display at 3840 × 2160 and 160 Hz, the median measured the same day was 8.3 ms; about 10 ms with the Windows app.
- **Out of the box**: a virtual display at each device's resolution and refresh rate (checked up to 3840 × 2160 at 160 Hz), the PC's own screens turned off during the session and back on at the end; sound in stereo, 5.1 or 7.1 depending on the device (Steam must be installed on the PC for its virtual speakers); variable refresh rate on Mac, Windows, Linux and Android phones; shared clipboard on desktop and mobile apps; 4:4:4 colour for sharp text on devices that decode it; up to four controllers, seen by the PC as Xbox controllers.
- **Resilience**: every app reconnects on its own after a network drop (ten attempts, one second apart); losses are corrected (forward error correction in the Game and Max profiles) and native apps ask for a full picture after a loss.
- **Controllers**: in KyberNow Admin, each device can have an app that opens on the PC when its session starts (Steam Big Picture, Playnite, Xbox, Epic, GOG and others are detected), closed at the end. The TV apps (Apple TV, Android TV, LG), the Steam Deck and KyberNow Link OS are navigated entirely with a controller, which can also act as a mouse on the Windows desktop; on Mac and iPhone/iPad the controller opens the session menu (L1 + R1 + Start + Select).
- **KyberNow Share**: share the computer with up to four guests, from the session bar or from the computer itself (choose the screen to show and keep using it). Guests join with a six-digit code, a link or a QR code, in a KyberNow Link app or in a browser, at home or from afar through the relay (the host accepts each guest who comes from the internet). A guest arrives as a spectator; the host gives them, separately, their controllers and the keyboard and mouse, and the Station enforces these rights. Each guest picks their own picture quality (Auto, same as the host, 4K 60 Hz, 1080p 60 Hz, 720p 30 Hz), never above the host's, without ever disturbing the host's picture. Dedicated page: https://www.kybernow.app/en/share/
- **Lending the computer** (part of KyberNow Share, since 0.9.0): hand the computer to someone while you are not using it, a relative who enjoys your gaming PC or a colleague who needs the workstation. Three ways: a six-digit code for one session (1, 2 or 4 hours, or until you take it back; the code is used once and valid 24 hours), friend accounts created in Admin (username, password, invitation link; the friend borrows when the computer is free, otherwise asks), and weekly time slots (during their slot the friend goes before the host, with 2 minutes' notice). The borrower plays or works from their own device in "console mode": a full-screen launcher that only shows the allowed apps (any app from the Start menu: game launchers such as Steam in Big Picture, Epic, GOG or Playnite, a single game, a work program), with the Steam account chosen per loan (theirs, with Steam family sharing, or the host's). Explorer, the Windows key, Alt+Tab, Task Manager, command prompts, Open/Save As dialogs and apps outside the list are blocked; a game can still read the disk, so lend to people you trust. The host takes the computer back with a 2-minute notice; afterwards apps close, Steam returns to the host's account, windows come back and the Windows session stays open. One loan at a time; the borrower can come back for 15 minutes after a dropped connection.
- **HDR** (since 0.9.1): on an HDR screen (a Mac's XDR display, an iPhone, an iPad, an HDR TV behind an Apple TV, an LG TV) an "HDR" chip on the computer card is on by default and remembered per computer; HDR games and Windows arrive as they are (HEVC Main 10 or AV1 10-bit, 4:2:0); the Station switches the virtual display to HDR at the start of the session and back at the end, and tells games the brightness of the device's screen; an "HDR calibration" screen offers four test patterns; a share guest without an HDR screen gets an SDR picture. Needs Windows 11 24H2 and a graphics card with a 10-bit encoder on the PC; a Mac Station does HDR with the Apple chip. Android, Windows and Linux apps: later.
- **PlayStation consoles** (since 0.9.5, all KyberNow Link apps): a PS5 or PS4 on your network appears on the home screen next to your computers, like Sony's Remote Play. Pair once with the 8-digit code shown by the console (Settings › System › Remote Play › Link Device) after signing in to the PlayStation Network account once (several accounts per device, several accounts per console); "Play" or "Wake and play"; picture up to 1080p at 60 fps (upscaled with adjustable sharpness on Apple devices), HDR on an HDR screen; full DualSense (adaptive triggers, rumble, touchpad, gyroscope; HD haptics over USB on Mac), keyboard and mouse standing in for a controller with a configurable layout; accounts and consoles follow Apple devices through iCloud and are sent to a TV or PC with a 6-digit code. Away from home through a VPN (add the console by address) or through the KyberNow relay with a Station switched on at home on the console's network; never through Sony's servers. KyberNow is not affiliated with Sony.
- **KyberNow accounts, families and teams** (since 0.10 beta, stable in 0.11): an optional account (email and password, passkeys, two-factor authentication), created and managed on share.kybernow.app (sign in: https://share.kybernow.app/compte/connexion?lang=en). Signed in to KyberNow Link, your computers appear on every device without pairing (TVs show a code approved from a phone). You link the Station from Admin or during installation, then open it to someone by email with rights: "Watch" (see the actual screen, no keyboard, mouse or controller, nothing changes for the host, who sees and can remove them), "Open the desktop", "Borrow to play", "Join your shares" (no code) and "Administer" (two-factor required). Families and teams have members with roles (Owner, Administrator, Member), groups of people, computer groups whose rights apply to present and future computers, a log of who opened what, and, for teams, enrolment tokens to deploy a whole fleet (silent install: KyberNow-Station-Setup.exe /quiet /enroll=<token> /relay=<address>). Also: single-use access links (valid 1, 7 or 30 days, revocable), invitations that expire after 30 days and can be resent, settings synced across devices (profile, video format, bitrate, sharp text, HDR, immersive mode; a switch in the app's settings), moving a computer between families and teams with a preview of who loses access, "Open Admin" from the account with a passkey (on the home network, or from anywhere once "Remote Admin" is switched on locally; 30-minute inactivity timeout), 2-minute access tokens, devices signed out after 90 days unused. Codes, sharing and lending keep working without an account.
- **PyroWave** (0.11): an extra picture format (wavelet-based, open source, MIT) compressed and decompressed in a fraction of a millisecond on the graphics card (Vulkan on a Windows PC, Metal on a Mac), at the cost of a high bitrate (about 300 Mbit/s at 1080p, 5 to 10 times HEVC). Chosen under "Video format"; "Auto" only picks it when the device is wired, never in a browser. If bandwidth is short, the app lowers resolution, then refresh rate, never sharpness, and says so; if the network saturates for 5 seconds, it offers "Switch to HEVC". Needs a Windows Station (Vulkan 1.3 graphics card) or Mac Station that offers it; on Raspberry Pi, only the Pi 5 decodes it. In full screen, the Mac app turns on macOS Game Mode.
- **Automatic bitrate** (0.11): with the bitrate on "Auto", the app lowers the bitrate when the network saturates (round-trip rise, packet loss, picture gaps; two strained seconds in a row, by 30%) and raises it back after clean seconds; a bitrate set by hand never moves; the Station changes bitrate without freezing the picture; the Statistics show the target bitrate ("42 / 60 Mbit/s · lowered, network saturated"). Paused with PyroWave; not yet in the browser.
- **Immersive mode** (0.11; Mac, Windows and Linux apps): the whole keyboard goes to the computer, system shortcuts included (⌘ Tab, ⌘ Space and Mission Control on a Mac; Alt+Tab and the Windows key on Windows and Linux); per-computer setting "In full screen" (default), "Always" or "Never"; the app's own shortcuts (⌃⌥⌘ or Ctrl+Alt+Shift + letter) stay with the app; on a Mac it asks once for the Accessibility permission, and ⌘ becomes the Windows key when facing a PC.
- **Pen** (0.11): pressure, tilt, eraser and pen button from a graphics tablet (Mac, Windows, Linux apps), an iPad's Apple Pencil or an Android stylus reach a Windows or Mac Station as a real pen; not yet in the browser.
- **KyberNow Station for Linux**: GNOME and KDE under Wayland, x86_64 and arm64, .deb and .rpm packages (KyberNow-Station-Linux-x86_64.deb, .rpm), NVIDIA, Intel and AMD encoding (VA-API) or the processor.
- **Three products**: KyberNow Station (on the Windows PC or Mac that streams), KyberNow Admin (the Station's settings, in the browser) and KyberNow Link (the apps that display the PC on your devices). "KyberNow" alone is the name of the whole project. Former names: KyberNow Server (now Station), the KyberNow console (now Admin), the KyberNow apps or clients (now Link).
- **KyberNow Station**: Windows 10 or 11, any graphics card (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, eGPU) or the processor. One installer (KyberNow-Station-Setup.exe) sets up the Kyber engine, KyberNow Admin, a virtual display and virtual speakers per session, the controller driver and the firewall (two ports chosen at install, plus local discovery). No online account required: a local name and password chosen at install (an optional KyberNow account can be linked, see above); devices pair with a six-digit code accepted in Admin. **KyberNow Station for Mac** (KyberNow-Station-Mac.dmg, signed and notarised): an Apple-silicon Mac on macOS 15 or later becomes a Station like a Windows PC, with the same Admin, a virtual display at each device's resolution (the Mac's screens off during the session), a KyberNow sound output (stereo, 5.1, 7.1), HDR, sharing and lending, updates from Admin; three macOS permissions at install (Screen Recording, Accessibility, Microphone for the virtual sound output); from a PC or TV the Windows key acts as ⌘ and the Keys menu offers the Mac combinations and "Ctrl acts as ⌘".
- **KyberNow Link**: your computer on all your devices. Native apps for Mac, Windows, Apple TV, iPhone, iPad, Android 11 or later (phones, tablets, Android TV and Google TV), LG TVs (webOS 5 or later, installed in developer mode), Linux (desktop, Steam Deck, SteamOS in the living room, as a Flatpak) and the Raspberry Pi (Pi 3, 4 and 5, as a .deb on 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS, or as **KyberNow Link OS**, an image written with Raspberry Pi Imager that boots straight into Link, with HDMI-CEC and whole-OS A/B updates on Pi 4 and 5). Apple TV and iPhone/iPad apps are on the App Store. A web version served by the Station itself works in a modern browser (stereo sound).
- **Versus Sunshine + Moonlight**: QUIC (RFC 9000) instead of GameStream; picture always encrypted; virtual display at the device's resolution built in; pairing through Bonjour, QR code or an on-screen code instead of a PIN; works in the browser too; HDR; guests and lending; relay for away from home; PlayStation consoles; optional accounts for families and teams; PyroWave on a wired home network.
- **For professionals**: sharp text in 4:4:4, 10-bit HDR, a real pen (pressure, tilt, rotation, eraser) from an iPad, an Android tablet or a graphics tablet, every screen of the device, several computers at once, microphone and webcam forwarded to the workstation, recordings kept on the Station; no fixed resolution cap other than the graphics card's encoder (5K at 60 Hz and 4K at 160 Hz tried). Teams get roles, groups of people and computers, a log, single-use access links, silent deployment with an enrolment token, enterprise sign-in (SSO and OAuth) and their own relay. Versus Parsec: free for teams (Parsec Teams and Enterprise are paid per user), open source, a Linux host too, beyond 4K at 60 Hz, HDR, 4:4:4 and pen included without a paid plan.
- **Price**: free, no account required, no subscription, no ads. Community, non-commercial project by Les Lignes Claires. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the Kyber team.

## Pages

- [Home (English)](https://www.kybernow.app/en/): what KyberNow is in one sentence, two entrances (Play, Work), how a picture travels in 9.4 ms, installing in three steps, the four apps (Station, Link, Share, Admin), free and open source
- [Play (English)](https://www.kybernow.app/en/play/): your computer's games on every screen (TV, tablet, phone, Steam Deck, another computer, a browser, a Raspberry Pi with KyberNow Link OS), PS5 and PS4, playing together and lending the computer, controllers, HDR, PyroWave, comparison with Sunshine + Moonlight
- [Work (English)](https://www.kybernow.app/en/pro/): your workstation wherever you are, 4:4:4 sharp text, HDR, pen, displays, four uses (creative studios, remote workstations, game studios, teams and fleets), team console, deployment, security (SSO and OAuth), comparison with Parsec, price
- [Download (English)](https://www.kybernow.app/en/download/): KyberNow Station for Windows, Mac and Linux, KyberNow Link for each device, pairing with a six-digit code
- [KyberNow Share (English)](https://www.kybernow.app/en/share/): playing together with up to four guests, lending the computer, families and teams with a KyberNow account, away from home through the relay
- [Technology (English)](https://www.kybernow.app/en/technology/): the measured trip of a picture, QUIC, the Kyber engine, comparison with Sunshine + Moonlight, PyroWave, features and profiles in detail
- [Guide (English)](https://www.kybernow.app/en/guide/): one article per task, from installing the Station to teams and the relay
- [FAQ (English)](https://www.kybernow.app/en/guide/faq/): frequently asked questions
- French versions: [Accueil](https://www.kybernow.app/), [Jouer](https://www.kybernow.app/jeu/), [Travailler](https://www.kybernow.app/pro/), [Télécharger](https://www.kybernow.app/telecharger/), [Share](https://www.kybernow.app/share/), [Technologie](https://www.kybernow.app/technologie/), [Guide](https://www.kybernow.app/guide/), [FAQ](https://www.kybernow.app/guide/faq/)
